title: Decision-Graph Contract Enforcer for Region/Tier Fallbacks
creator: Aisha Verma
description: Add a decision-graph based contract enforcer that validates routing rules at both config-compile time and runtime. This ticket covers: (1) a deterministic graph generation step that converts DSL routing rules into a decision graph for region/tier/variant selection; (2) a rules contract verifier that checks for unreachable branches, unsafe fallbacks (e.g. cross-variant KV incompatibility), and non-deterministic routing loops; (3) a staged migration mode to allow rolling updates of the validator without breaking existing configs; and (4) runtime lightweight guards that enforce critical invariants when the compiled policy is executed.
acceptance_criteria: Generate a canonical decision graph from the existing routing DSL for 95% of real configs (edge cases documented)
Detect and fail config uploads that contain: unreachable nodes, fallback-to-incompatible-variant, or circular routing decisions with clear error messages and remediation hints
Provide a --staged-migration flag that permits warn-only validation for a configurable set of namespaces for 2 weeks
Add unit and integration tests covering region-tier fallbacks across CPU/GPU/quantized variants and verify KV cache compatibility checks
Expose a console view with per-rule validation results and links to offending config lines
tech_notes: Decision graph generation will occur in the config compiler module. Graph nodes represent decision predicates (region, tier, model-variant compatibility) and edges represent fallback transitions.
Compatibility matrix: add an explicit compatibility table between variant families (float16, int8, q4) to prevent fallback to variants that lose required KV schema.
Staged migration: validator has three modes: strict (fail), warn, and off. Default for new installs is warn for 2 cycles, then strict after opt-in.
Runtime guards: add O(1) checks for critical invariants (e.g., model shard availability, region affinity override) to avoid policy-engine panics when external state changes.
Performance: graph generation should complete in <50ms for typical 30-rule configs. Use memoization and shallow clone of predicates to avoid allocations.
Telemetry: emit validation.summary events and per-violation metrics (violation_type, namespace, config_id) for alerting and rollout decisions.
implementation_plan: Spike: implement a prototype graph generator + three small test configs (2d)
Design review: present graph model and error taxonomy to Eng + PM + DX (1d)
Core implementation: compiler adapter, contract checks, and migration flag (5d)
Tests: unit tests, fuzz harness for random rules, integration e2e with console (3d)
Rollout: enable warn-only for internal namespaces, monitor telemetry for 2 weeks, iterate on error messages (2w)
Hardening: add runtime guards and SLA-safe fallback behavior, finalize docs and console surface (1w)
dsl_examples:
# Example routing rule that demonstrates region preference with tier fallback:
region: [eu-west-1, us-east-1]
tier: { premium -> reserved -> shared }
fallbacks:
  - to_variant: quantized-q4_0 if compatibility(model_family, 'q4')
  - to_variant: float16_default
# This should become a graph with nodes: region_choice -> tier_choice -> variant_compat_check -> fallback_edge

# Invalid config example the enforcer should catch:
region: [us-west-2]
tier: { shared -> reserved }
fallbacks:
  - to_variant: int8_beta # int8_beta is incompatible with current KV layout -> validator must error
